# 编译原理实验-文法分析器（Parser）![](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-cpp-green.svg)

## Table of Contents

- [Background](#background)
- [Install](*install)
- [Usage](*usage)
- [Related Efforts](#related-efforts)
- [Maintainers](#maintainers)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)



## Background

**语法分析器**（Parser）通常是作为[编译器](https://baike.baidu.com/item/编译器/8853067)或[解释器](https://baike.baidu.com/item/解释器/10418965)的组件出现的，它的作用是进行语法检查、并构建由输入的单词组成的数据结构（一般是[语法分析树](https://baike.baidu.com/item/语法分析树/20452541)、[抽象语法树](https://baike.baidu.com/item/抽象语法树/6129952)等层次化的数据结构）。语法分析器通常使用一个独立的[词法分析器](https://baike.baidu.com/item/词法分析器/4336210)从输入字符流中分离出一个个的“单词”，并将单词流作为其输入。实际开发中，语法分析器可以手工编写，也可以使用工具（半）自动生成。

现要求设计一个LL(1)语法分析器，能够根据用户所输入的二型文法构造出其对应的LL(1)分析表，并能够判断出用户所输入的某个串是否是该文法所产生的句子

### 要求

**1**、用户在一个TXT文件中输入一个二型文法，要求如下：

- 1）文法中的终结符和非终结符各不少于2个
- 2）必须至少有1条文法规则的右部出现ε（用户以输入“@”代表输入“ε”）
- 3）文法共计至少4条规则，且至少1条规则的右部必须有2个及以上的符号
- 4）必须至少有1条规则不是“左线性”或“右线性”文法
- 5）必须至少有1个非终结符有2个或2个以上的产生式
- 6）没有冗余的文法规则，文法要能够完整地推导出某个语言

**2**、系统读取该TXT文件，展示出每条文法右部符号串的**First**集（重复的只需展示**1**次）以及每个   **非终结符**的**Follow**集。

**3、**展示出该文法所对应的**LL(1)分析表**

**4**、用户输入一个由终结符组成的字符串，系统展示出分析过程，并给出分析结论（该串“是”或“不是”文法的句子）。请分别使用**2**个字符串进行测试，分别让系统显示出“该串是文法的句子”和“该串不是文法的句子”的结论

### 流程设计

##### 设计步骤流程描述

1、读入原程序；

2、从原程序中提取规则、非终结符、终结符、右部，并输出；

3、对于提取出的右部、非终结符，分别对他们求First集和Follow集；

4、根据提取出来的终结符、非终结符、规则以及相应的First集和Follow集构建LL（1）分析表；

5、根据构建好的分析表结构，要求用户输入字符串，并分析是否符合文法； 

##### 设计步骤流程图

![img](https://i.loli.net/2021/05/01/3cStjIFw2J4ykXP.png)

### 设计过程

设计过程将从数据需求着手，分析制定合理简约的数据结构，以确保代码易读、优雅。

**数据结构：**

- 1、规则-结构体：考虑到数据存储和输出，需要为常用数据—规则定义专用数据结构，主要分为两部分，一部分是左部，由于至多一个字符，故用字符类型定义；一部分是右部，由于右部有可能有好几种选择，故用一个字符串动态数组定义，又考虑到规则需要经常被输出，于是重载输出流操作符；

  ```cpp
  struct rule {
  	char left;                 //规则左部 
  	vector<string> right;        //规则右部
  	friend ostream& operator << (ostream& out, rule rule);//重载输出流操作符
  };
  ```

- 2、F（irst/ollow）集-结构体：考虑到要格式化输出First/Follow集，又考虑到这两类集数据结构基本相似，于是为这两类数据定义一个通用的数据结构，并通过一个判别符is_first加以区分，并在重载的输出流操作符函数里根据该判别符输出不同的提示信息；

  ```cpp
  struct F_set {
  	bool is_first;              //First集 or Follow集判别符
  	string left;              //F集左部
  	set<char> right;          //F集右部
  	friend ostream& operator << (ostream& out, F_set f_set);//重载输出流操作符
  };
  ```

- 3、LL（1）分析表-结构体：考虑到要格式化输出分析表，仅用一个动态数组存放规则显然是不够的，于是定义如下结构体， 在数组之外，指明表格的横纵表头，并通过重载输出流操作符进行格式化输出，也使得主函数简单、易读；

  ```cpp
  struct LL_1_table {
  	vector<char> row;          //行表头数组
  	vector<char> col;           //列表头数组
      vector<rule> rules;          //规则数组
  	friend ostream& operator << (ostream& out, LL_1_table table);//重载输出流操作符
  };
  ```

##### 功能实现描述

功能实现主要分为文件读写模块、主要元素提取模块、First集求取模块、Follow集求取模块、LL(1)分析表构建模块、文法合规判断模块这六大模块，分别完成程序预处理功能、求First、Follow集、构建分析表、文法合规判断的任务。单词-类别信息数据结构：

![img](https://i.loli.net/2021/05/01/r7uQi1jWfyRF53A.png)

scores.notes: Best measured parse-correctness: 59/59 units, 34/36 e2e, terminates on every pathological grammar I threw at it (exit 0 with the 10000-step cap). Last-write-wins conflict policy is the one that happens to satisfy both shipped pathological cases (S::=Sa|b + 'b', A::=B B::=A|c + 'c'). Two real defects: the '@'-inside-a-right-part bug (A::=a@b + 'ab' wrongly rejected) and the shared 'ad#' false accept. Q5 is far and away the best answer of the four -- a full 59-line output map with provenance per line, and I confirmed the load-bearing structural claims (59 lines total, 68-byte table rows, 60-byte trace rows, blank-line positions, trailing-space columns) are all exactly right. Two doc errors in that same section: it claims all three test*.txt end in a newline (none do -- last bytes are '@', ' ', 'e'), and roughly eight of its per-line byte counts are undercounted (line 1 is 38 not 34, line 20 is 29 not 26, line 29 is 30 not 28). Correctly reported the run_parser.sh 'cp x x' abort. Style is house style exactly: default-right setw, tabs, Chinese comments, ostringstream-before-setw explained. Note this design is effectively the code already committed at HEAD, so it adds little novelty -- but through a parse-correctness lens it measures best.

Ties formats on the e2e count (34/36) but has a strictly worse failure mode: it does not terminate. It deliberately relegates the loop cap to 'Optional hardening, not required by the lab', so grammar S::=b|Sa with input 'b' runs until killed (exit 124 after 30 s), emitting trace rows without bound while the analysis stack grows one symbol per step. S::=b|S does the same. Every other design terminates on both. Its own reasoning ('None of test1/test2/test3 can reach this') is true but the repo has a dedicated pathological-grammar test class. Also carries the '@'-in-middle bug and the 'ad#' false accept. Q3 proof is the cleanest prose argument of the four and its reachability analysis of the spurious [G,#] cell is correct. Verification-integrity ding: the 'real run' excerpt for test1 input '(a' is labelled steps 9 and 10; the actual steps are 6 and 7 -- the format is exact, the numbers are not. It also lists 'run_parser.sh test3.txt aaabd' among its test invocations, which aborted before the build in the state it was written against.

The best engineering, the wrong recommendation. It is the ONLY design that skips '@' char-by-char when pushing the RHS, so it alone passes A::=a@b + 'ab' -- and HEAD has since adopted exactly that fix, vindicating the call. Its fixpoint FIRST/FOLLOW is genuinely correct and I measured 0.017 s vs 3.2-3.4 s for the guarded-recursion designs on the 20-non-terminal chain, so the exponential diagnosis is real. But it recommends keep-first conflict resolution, which regresses two cases the repo explicitly tests (S::=Sa|b + 'b' and A::=B B::=A|c + 'c' both flip to rejected), dropping it to 33/36. To its credit it is the only design that correctly states the symmetry -- reversing to S::=b|Sa flips which policy wins -- and I confirmed that empirically; it just picked the side that loses the shipped tests. Also carries the 'ad#' false accept: its unknown-symbol pre-check cannot catch it because '#' is a legitimate column. Fidelity ding: parser_first_core says 'the recursive core' and parser_follow_core says 'recurse to parent FOLLOW sets', and its recommended code removes recursion entirely (it does offer the recursive variant as option (a)). Its MAX_STEP of 500+100*|w| is much tighter than the others; I could not construct a realistic false-reject but the margin is thin. Correctly flagged the terminal.insert('#') aliasing and verified no conflict warning fires on the three shipped grammars (I confirmed: 0, 0, 0).

Worst measured parse-correctness of the four: 32/36. It stacks both discriminating defects -- keep-first (loses S::=Sa|b + 'b' and A::=B B::=A|c + 'c') AND the '@'-in-middle bug (loses A::=a@b + 'ab') -- plus the shared 'ad#' false accept. Its own claim that 'the lab's grammars never hit' the conflict path is falsified by two cases already in test_parser_e2e.sh. Also the slowest by a wide margin at 6.81 s on the 20-NT chain, roughly 2x the other recursive designs, because it hoists findFollow(rules[i].left) outside the candidate loop and pays for FOLLOW on every rule whether or not any candidate is nullable. Style: 'cout << left' deviates from the sibling lexer, which uses default-right setw at LexicalAnalysis.cpp:268 and :274 -- more readable output, but the brief asked to copy that file's style. Genuine strengths that keep fidelity high: the per-clause requirement mapping is the most rigorous of the four (it walks each yaml phrase to the line that implements it), the Q3 evidence is the strongest offered by anyone (a brute-force differential over every string up to length 5 against a textbook-FOLLOW build, 0 verdict differences), and it correctly reported the run_parser.sh 'cp x x' abort and the terminal.insert('#') aliasing.

criticalFlaws: SHARED BY ALL FOUR -- false ACCEPT of a non-sentence. Grammar test3 (E::=aH H::=aMd|d M::=Ab|@ A::=aM|e), input 'ad#'. All four print 字符串ad#是该文法的句子. '#' is pushed as an ordinary input character, so after E::=aH / match a / H::=d / match d the analysis stack is '#' and the input top is the USER's '#', and the top=='#' && cur=='#' accept branch fires. This is the most severe class of parser bug (accepting a string outside the language) and no design mentions it. Robust's unknown-symbol pre-check does not catch it because '#' is a legitimate column. HEAD has since fixed it with an explicit input.find('#') guard.

faithful -- NON-TERMINATION with unbounded memory growth. Grammar 'S::=b|Sa', input 'b'. Measured exit=124 (killed) after 30 s; also 'S::=b|S' + 'b', exit=124. The design places the step cap under 'Optional hardening, not required by the lab', so the parse loop has no bound. With last-write-wins, [S,b] holds S::=Sa; each iteration pops S and pushes 'a','S', so the analysis stack grows by one symbol per step forever while print_state emits a row (and rebuilds the whole growing string) each time. Every other design terminates on both grammars. formats, with the same conflict policy, terminates at exit 0 via its 10000-step cap.

faithful and formats and spec -- '@' inside a right part is pushed onto the analysis stack. The guard is the whole-string test if (right != "@"). Grammar 'A::=a@b', input 'ab'. All three print 字符串ab不是该文法的句子; correct is 是. Trace: [A,a]=A::=a@b, push reverse -> stack #b@a, match 'a', then stack top '@' is not a row header so it is treated as a terminal and compared against lookahead 'b' -> mismatch. Robust is the only design that gets this right (it skips '@' character-by-character), and HEAD has since adopted robust's fix.

robust and spec -- keep-first conflict resolution regresses two acceptance cases the repo explicitly tests. robust's fill_cell and spec's occupancy check both refuse to overwrite an occupied cell. Grammar 'S::=Sa|b', input 'b' -> both print 字符串b不是该文法的句子 (correct: 是); grammar 'A::=B  B::=A|c', input 'c' -> both print 字符串c不是该文法的句子 (correct: 是). Both are named cases in /workspace/agent_tests/test_parser_e2e.sh under the comment 病态文法不能让分析器崩溃或者死循环. In both, keep-first parks the self-referential production (S::=Sa, B::=A) in the cell and the parse spins until the step cap trips. I verified by patching only this one policy into an otherwise-passing build: 28 cases, exactly 2 failures, both of these.

spec -- worst aggregate parse-correctness: it is the only design carrying BOTH the keep-first regression and the '@'-in-middle bug, so it fails 4 of 36 e2e cases (S::=Sa|b + 'b', A::=B B::=A|c + 'c', A::=a@b + 'ab', test3 + 'ad#'), against 2 for formats and faithful and 3 for robust.
